body_html:
How to think about it

Clothes are made from fibres. Natural fibres come from plants (cotton, jute, linen, coir) and animals (wool, silk); synthetic fibres such as nylon and polyester are made from chemicals from petroleum. Cotton is picked, ginned to remove seeds, spun into yarn, woven on a loom, dyed or printed and stitched into clothes.

India's weavers make famous handloom cloth: Banarasi silk, Kanjeevaram silk, Pochampally ikat and Pashmina shawls. We choose clothes to suit the weather and work, and we reuse old clothes as bags, quilts and dusters.

Example

Removing seeds from cotton is…

the step after picking

Answer: ginning

Example

Kanjeevaram silk is from…

Kanchipuram

Answer: Tamil Nadu

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up spinning and weaving.
  • Thinking silk is a plant fibre.
  • Wearing synthetic clothes near fire.

faq.q: What is the difference between weaving and knitting?
faq.a: Weaving crosses two sets of yarn on a loom; knitting makes cloth from a single yarn using needles or a machine.

faq.q: Why is cotton good for summer?
faq.a: It absorbs sweat and lets air pass through, keeping us cool.
